flags.summary: StorybookDecorator.tsx wraps stories in ThemeProvider only, with no CssBaseline.
flags.effect: The global :focus-visible outline (0.17.1) and MUI's box-sizing reset never apply in Storybook although they do in the app. Storybook is not a faithful renderer of the shipped result.
flags.handling: Independent confirmation that reading source, not rendering, is the correct method.

flags.summary: packages/billing-system pins @kareo-engineering/design-system 0.6.0 while the workspace package is 0.18.3.
flags.effect: A live consumer frozen one release before the 0.7.0 palette migration — i.e. still on the pre-process palette. Its two stories are not a token source.
flags.handling: Excluded.

flags.summary: ToggleButtonOverrides.ts contains a '&$disabled' rule written in JSS v4 ref syntax. Emotion does not compile it, so the plain disabled state has never received Tebra's treatment.
flags.shipping: MUI's own '&.Mui-disabled': color action.disabled rgba(0,0,0,0.5), border 1px action.disabledBackground rgba(0,0,0,0.12).
flags.note: The neighbouring '&.Mui-selected.Mui-disabled' in the SAME file is written correctly and does execute, so a disabled SELECTED toggle gets grey[400] on white while a disabled UNSELECTED one does not. The two disabled states in one component disagree because of a one-character-class typo.
flags.handling: Built as it ships. Second dead-code finding in the override set after MuiRadioButton; that one was an invalid key, this one is invalid selector syntax, so a key-validity sweep would not have caught it.

flags.summary: Hovering a selected ToggleButton discards Tebra's action.selected #F0EEE8 and renders MUI's computed rgba(0,0,0,0.12) instead.

cascade.tebra: '&.Mui-selected' — specificity (0,2,0), appended after the base so it wins at rest
cascade.mui: '&.Mui-selected:hover' — specificity (0,3,0), which no same-slot override can beat

flags.handling: Both states built as they resolve. Fixing this in code needs the override to carry its own selected:hover rule, exactly as ChipOverrides does for the chip.

flags.summary: SvgIconOverrides.ts's fontSizeSmall / Medium / Large are exact rem restatements of MUI's own pxToRem(20 | 24 | 35) AFTER the 16/14 inflation, so all three are no-ops.
flags.consequence: This is the clearest evidence in the codebase that the pxToRem inflation was transcribed rather than intended: someone read the computed values out of a browser and pasted them back as literals. The file's real content is the three ADDED sizes — fontSizeXxsmall 0.75rem, fontSizeXsmall 1rem, fontSizeSmaller 1.25rem — which are honest px and carry no inflation.
flags.affects: Every icon in every component. Icons encoded as 20 / 24 / 35 render 22.857 / 27.429 / 40. Intended integers are bound in Figma; computedPx recorded per component.
flags.handling: Reported. Nothing rebuilt — the file changes nothing today, but deleting the three restated keys would be a safe no-op cleanup and would make the inflation visible.

flags.summary: AvatarOverrides.ts registers MuiAvatar with defaultProps {} and styleOverrides {} — every rule is commented out. Avatar is 100% substrate.
flags.correction: The coverage sweep classified Avatar as content 'both' and expect 'themed'. That was wrong: the file has a valid key and executes, but contributes nothing.
flags.theTodo: // TODO: handle set sizing and box shadow for disabled elevation — neither half is done. The story passes args { disableElevation: true }, but Avatar has no disableElevation prop, so the arg spreads onto the div and paints nothing. The story is written against an intent that was never implemented.
flags.handling: Built as pure substrate. The empty override and the inert story arg are both recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: ToggleButtonGroupVariations iterates sizes ['large','default','small']. 'default' is not a valid MUI ToggleButton size.
consequences: size='default' matches neither the sizeSmall nor the sizeLarge branch, so the button silently renders MEDIUM padding while carrying a MuiToggleButton-sizeDefault class that styles nothing.

The same string reaches <SvgIcon fontSize='default'>, which indexes MUI's { inherit, small, medium, large } map to undefined and matches no Tebra override either — so that icon has NO font-size rule and falls back to inheriting the button's 16px, instead of the 27.429px a real medium icon would be.
The story's own state maps are keyed large / medium / small, so exclusiveAlignment['default'] and multiFormat['default'] are permanently undefined and the middle group's selection never persists.
flags.handling: Built as Medium with the correct medium icon. Story bug, not a component bug — recorded in the description.

flags.summary: Four override entries set a value MUI already uses, so they change nothing. Three were found in this batch.

instances.TabsOverrides.tsx: defaultProps.indicatorColor = 'primary' — MUI's Tabs already defaults indicatorColor to 'primary'. It is the file's only content, so TabsOverrides contributes nothing visible at all.
instances.MobileStepperOverrides.ts: dotActive.backgroundColor = primary.main — MUI already uses primary.main for the active dot. The same file DOES change root background and dot colour, so it is not a no-op file.
instances.DialogOverrides.ts: restates MUI's own maxWidth default — recorded earlier, in the Dialog component description.
instances.SvgIconOverrides.ts: the three restated font sizes — see svgIconOverridesRestateTheInflatedValues.

flags.handling: Reported. Harmless, but they make the theme look larger than it is: an override file existing is not evidence that a component is themed.

flags.summary: In a linear Stepper every step after the active one is marked '.Mui-disabled', but StepLabel's Label slot defines no disabled rule — so an upcoming step is pixel-identical to a plain inactive step.
flags.detail: StepLabelLabel styles only .Mui-active, .Mui-completed, .Mui-error and .Mui-alternativeLabel. StepLabelRoot's only disabled rule is cursor: default. StepIcon's root colour (text.disabled #9A9A9A) applies to anything that is neither active, completed nor error, so it covers the disabled case by falling through rather than by naming it.
flags.consequence: One appearance, two semantics: an upcoming linear step and an unvisited non-linear step render the same. Nothing in the UI says a step is unreachable.
flags.handling: Built as a single 'Default' variant, named for the appearance rather than the class. Recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: StepConnector adds .Mui-active and .Mui-completed classes to its line and then defines no styles for either, so every connector is grey[400] #D6D6D6 regardless of progress.
flags.detail: StepConnectorLine's only colour is `theme.palette.mode === 'light' ? grey[400] : grey[600]`. Tebra has no StepConnector override. A completed run of steps therefore has no visual through-line.
flags.handling: Built at one colour. Reported as a design gap rather than a defect — MUI ships the hooks, nobody used them.

flags.summary: ToggleButton adds two more disabled treatments to the sibling set, and its two disagree with each other.

disabled.Radio: action.disabled rgba(0,0,0,0.5) — substrate, dead override key
disabled.ToggleButton (unselected): action.disabled rgba(0,0,0,0.5) with an rgba(0,0,0,0.12) border — substrate, dead JSS selector
disabled.ToggleButton (selected): grey[400] #D6D6D6 on common.white — Tebra, the one rule in the file that compiles

flags.note: Two of the five land on action.disabled only because their Tebra rule failed to execute. Fixing either dead rule would change the count, not settle it.
flags.handling: All built as they ship. Reported, not harmonised.

flags.summary: Three places in the library ask for a 500 weight that Akkurat LL cannot supply, and all three ship Regular.

sites.Autocomplete group label: MUI ListSubheader, fontWeightMedium — recorded earlier in namingFreeze.carriedForward

flags.consequence: A Stepper active label, a completed label and an inactive label are typographically identical and differ only in colour. All three sites sit OUTSIDE the typography.ts ramp, so no text style carries the note.
flags.handling: Built at Regular, which is what renders. Recorded in each component description.

flags.summary: Avatar's image path cannot be built: it needs a Figma image fill, and the plugin API available here forbids createImageAsync.
flags.handling: Three content variants built (Fallback, Letter, Icon) and the img case documented in the description as the same 40px circle with an object-fit: cover image fill. Honest omission, not a silent one.

flags.summary: The built arc is CircularProgress's declared resting dasharray, not a frame sampled from its animation.
flags.detail: Source comment: 'Some default value that looks fine waiting for the animation to kicks in' — strokeDasharray '80px, 200px', dashoffset 0. 80 of the 126.920 circumference is 63.03% of the ring, starting at 3 o'clock where an SVG <circle> path starts. In the product the arc simultaneously rotates (1.4s linear) and cycles its dasharray (1.4s ease-in-out).
flags.handling: Built at the declared state and labelled as such. No value was measured from a browser.

flags.summary: The Cover page inventory is frozen at roughly the tier-2 state and now contradicts the file it introduces.
flags.where: Cover page, Inventory and Not yet rebuilt sections (page 118:250).
flags.detail: Cover lists 9 component sets (Button through Autocomplete / Tag) against 39 in namingFreeze; "Icons — 12 components" against 31 masters on the Icons page; "Variables — 94" against 112 (Tebra/Color 64 + Typography 17 + Dimension 31); "23 recorded flags" against 89. Its Not yet rebuilt section still says ButtonGroup has "no canonical component here" though Button group / Segment is built, and open decision 4 still reads "Card is not built" though Card is built. The five open decisions themselves are transcribed verbatim and are still correct as decisions — only the build-status annotations after them have drifted.
flags.effect: The Cover is the reviewer-facing entry point per figmaBuild conventions, and it is the one page in the file that misstates the file. Publish is next in the queue, so a reviewer would meet the stale numbers first. Resolved before publish, as intended.
flags.handling: Reported, not rewritten. The Inventory and the build-status annotations are mechanically regenerable from the file; the Not yet rebuilt prose involves a judgement about what counts as deferred, so it is left for Daniel to sequence.
flags.resolution: Cover refreshed from live file state. Inventory now reads: nine pages; 31 component sets carrying 436 variants, 10 single-component composites, 38 icon and illustration masters (484 masters total); 10 text styles; 7 effect styles; 116 variables (Tebra/Color 67, Tebra/Typography 17, Tebra/Dimension 32); 105 flags. The 'Not yet rebuilt' section was rebuilt from coverageSweep.classification.DEFER and .PATTERN rather than prose, and the false ButtonGroup claim was dropped — Button group / Segment ships 54 variants. Three build-status annotations in Known drift were corrected: Radio's reference frame now points at the Reference page, 'Card is not built' became 'Card is built (2 variants)', and the Chip hardcoded-hex annotation was corrected against the live variable collection. All five decisions themselves remain OPEN and verbatim.

regression.method: Live per-page walk compared against the Cover's own Inventory text, read from node 118:261 rather than from the 2026-08-03 resolution note.
regression.coverSays: 31 component sets carrying 436 variants, 10 single-component composites, 38 icon and illustration masters (484 masters in all); Icons & illustrations — 31 icon masters, 7 illustration masters; Reference — 17 frames; Variables — 116 across Tebra/Color 67, Tebra/Typography 17, Tebra/Dimension 32; 105 recorded flags.
regression.fileSays: 34 component sets carrying 444 variants, 60 single-component masters, 504 component nodes in all; Icons & illustrations — 40 icon masters, 7 illustration masters (47); Reference — 19 frames; Variables — 120 across Tebra/Color 71, Tebra/Typography 17, Tebra/Dimension 32; 134 flags in the schema.
regression.worstPart: The Surfaces & navigation line omits the entire Primary nav (partner theme) section — Nav / Bar, Nav / Icon button, Nav / Menu item, Nav / Dropdown, Nav / Logo and Nav / Search are absent from the Cover, so the one family built from a different theme is the one a reviewer cannot see listed. The Reference line also predates the Deliberately not here frame it now holds.
regression.cause: The 2026-08-03 refresh was correct when written. Three batches landed after it — the nav build, the nav glyph and bar rebuild, and the review pass — and none regenerated the Cover. This is the same failure mode the Tokens page had before tokens-page-generator.js existed: a hand-maintained derived surface with no generator.
regression.handling: Reported, not rewritten — regenerating the Cover was not in this batch's scope and Daniel sequences the work. Recommended fix is a cover-page-generator.js alongside tokens-page-generator.js so the surface stops going stale between batches rather than being re-fixed each time.

flags.summary: Every illustration in the design system is drawn in #004952, which is not the palette teal. paletteValues primary.main, primary.dark, info.dark, action.active and action.focus are all #004852 (growth 1).
flags.where: All seven SVGs in src/components/illustrations. 405 of the 490 colour usages across the set.
flags.detail: The two differ by one step in the green channel: 0x48 = 72 vs 0x49 = 73. A grep for 004852 across the illustrations directory returns zero files, so no illustration ever uses the palette value. The difference is visually imperceptible, but it is the reason the art cannot bind to color/primary/main without changing a rendered value.
flags.effect: The dominant brand colour of the illustration set is off-token. Any future attempt to recolour illustrations from the palette produces a diff on 405 paths, and any audit assuming the illustrations use brand tokens is wrong.
flags.handling: Built as it ships. Promoted to color/hardcoded (no palette)/illustrationTeal so every path still binds and the value renders red on the generated Tokens page, which is the established mechanism for a colour with no palette entry. Not silently snapped to #004852 — that would change rendered output.

flags.summary: #F8F3EB appears once, in NothingToSeeHereIllustration, and matches no palette entry.
flags.detail: The nearest palette neighbours are action.selected #F0EEE8 (backbone 2) and background.default #E8E5DF (backbone 3). It is neither. The naming pattern suggests a backbone 1 that paletteValues.ts does not define.
flags.handling: Bound to color/hardcoded (no palette)/illustrationCream. Reported, not normalised.

flags.summary: Three ReadMore stories pass isInline where the component prop is $isInline, so the inline behaviour they document never happens.
flags.where: ReadMoreAlert.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxCharacters.stories.tsx args, ReadMoreMaxLines.stories.tsx argTypes.
flags.detail: ReadMoreProps extends EllipsisTextProps, which declares $isInline, $maxLines and $maxCharacters — the $ prefix keeps them off the DOM. Story args are assigned as a plain property on the story function and are never checked against ReadMoreProps, so the unprefixed spelling compiles silently. With $isInline undefined, EllipsisText renders display: -webkit-box rather than inline, and the leading space before the button — gated on ($isInline || !isCollapsed) — is skipped too.
flags.effect: Two of the four ReadMore stories carry a docblock stating that the button sits inline with the text on a single line. That is not what renders; the button drops onto its own line.
flags.handling: To be built as it ships, with the button on its own line. The intended inline arrangement is described in the component description but not depicted, because no story actually produces it.

flags.summary: NotFoundErrorMessage renders "submit a support caseor contact customer support" — the space between the link and the following sentence is lost.
flags.detail: The source closes at the end of one line and continues "or contact customer support" on the next. JSX strips newlines adjacent to a tag, so the two text runs concatenate with no separator. Both siblings get this right with an explicit {" "}: InternalServerErrorMessage after each , ForbiddenErrorMessage after its . NotFoundErrorMessage is the only one of the three that omits it.
flags.handling: To be built with the space present — depicting a text bug as a design decision would be worse. Flagged for the bug list.

flags.summary: ForbiddenErrorMessage links with a raw <a> while its siblings use MUI <Link>, and the package styles no <a> at all, so the two render in different colours.
flags.where: ForbiddenErrorMessage.tsx (raw <a> to the Tebra Help Center) against NotFoundErrorMessage.tsx and InternalServerErrorMessage.tsx (MUI <Link>).
flags.detail: There is no MuiLink override in src/overrides, and CssBaselineOverrides defines only *:focus-visible and *:focus:not(:focus-visible) — no anchor rule anywhere in the package. A raw <a> therefore falls to the user-agent default, conventionally #0000EE with a solid underline, while MUI Link resolves to primary.main #004852 underlined at alpha 0.4. The same sentence pattern, two link treatments, in sibling components of one family.
flags.handling: Both to be built as they resolve. Reported as a disagreement, not harmonised.

flags.summary: InternalServerErrorMessage ships <Link>contact support</Link> with no href, directly below a TODO saying the link is missing.
flags.detail: MUI Link without href renders an anchor with no href: not focusable, not keyboard-reachable, but still carrying full link styling. The comment immediately above reads "TODO: Add a link to the contact support".
flags.handling: To be built as styled text, matching what renders. Recorded in the component description.

flags.summary: ReadMore asks for color="inherit" but the theme forces primary.main at rest, so "inherit" only takes effect on hover — the label goes from teal to black.
flags.detail: MUI sets color: inherit in its base styled() when color="inherit". Tebra ButtonOverrides.text sets color: primary.main and is appended after the base at equal specificity, so the theme wins at rest. StyledButton then adds "&&:hover, &&:active { color: inherit }", whose doubled specificity wins it back on hover. The result is a resting label at #004852 that turns text.primary #000 on hover, over the primary[100] #CBDDE0 hover background the same theme rule supplies.
flags.effect: A colour inversion on hover that nobody appears to have chosen: the component asked for inherit in every state and receives it in exactly one.
flags.handling: Both states to be built as they resolve.

flags.summary: The six Feedback messages share one skeleton and disagree on nearly every measurement in it.
flags.detail: Stack marginTop is 0 (NoResults, NotFound), 16 (NothingToSeeHere) or 24 (Forbidden, InternalServerError, BrowserIncompatibility). Stack spacing is 8 (NoResults, NothingToSeeHere) or 16 (the other four). An h4 text.secondary eyebrow above the title is present in three (NotFound, Forbidden, InternalServerError) and absent in three. The h2 title carries sx maxWidth 45ch in three (NoResults, NothingToSeeHere, BrowserIncompatibility) and no constraint in the other three, while all six constrain the body to 75ch. Two carry an action Button, four carry none. One writes padding={5} where the other five write p={5}.
flags.handling: All six to be built as they ship, as six values of one Variant axis. Reported as the disagreement set, not normalised — the fourth recurring-surface finding after the four list-row surfaces, the five interactive states and the five disabled greys.

flags.summary: The Illustrations stories pass width/height whose aspect ratio does not match the viewBox, so the catalogue renders the art squashed — while the Feedback messages size the same art proportionally.
flags.where: src/stories/Illustrations/*.stories.tsx args against the Box dimensions in src/components/Feedback/*.tsx.
flags.detail: NotFoundIllustration has a 524x440 viewBox, ratio 1.191. Its story passes width 285 / height 184, ratio 1.549. The SVGs declare no width or height of their own, only a viewBox, so an outermost svg stretches to whatever box it is given. The messages avoid this: NotFound is sized 337x283 (64.3% of the viewBox, ratio preserved), NothingToSeeHere 455x262 (96%, preserved), and AccessRestricted, Error and BrowserIncompatibility are sized to their viewBox exactly.
flags.handling: Masters built at the viewBox — the undistorted shape, and the one the product actually renders. The story sizes are recorded but not built.

flags.summary: Of the seven illustrations, two are unused by any Feedback message, two have no Storybook story, and one serves two different messages.
flags.detail: AlmostThere and Waiting are exported and unused inside the design system; both are consumed downstream by signin-ui and clinical-notes-ui. Waiting and BrowserIncompatibility have no story, and BrowserIncompatibility is the only illustration used by a message yet missing from the catalogue. NotFoundIllustration serves both NotFoundErrorMessage and NoResultsMessage, so a "no results" state shows the 404 artwork.
flags.handling: All seven built as masters, since all seven are exported from the package. The usage map is recorded in each component description.

flags.summary: The Feedback message text widths are declared in ch, a unit with no Figma equivalent and no value derivable from component source.
flags.where: sx maxWidth 45ch on three titles and 75ch on all six bodies.
flags.detail: 1ch is the advance width of the digit zero in the element own computed font, so 45ch at h2 24px and 75ch at body1 16px are two different pixel values, both dependent on Akkurat LL metrics. Deriving them means reading a font metric rather than a component value; measuring them in a browser is forbidden by the method.
flags.handling: Unresolved. The honest options are to bind a fixed text width and record it as a Figma-only approximation, or to let the text hug and document the constraint. Deferred to the resumed batch rather than guessed.

flags.summary: InternalServerErrorMessage onRefreshClick builds a URLSearchParams, deletes redirectUrl from it, then discards it and calls window.location.reload().
flags.detail: The computed searchParams is never read again and never written back to the location, so the redirectUrl stripping has no effect — the reload preserves the query string the code was trying to clean.
flags.handling: No visual consequence. Recorded for the bug list.

flags.summary: The Figma family pages file five components differently from the Storybook titles those same components ship under.
flags.where: Figma figmaBuild.pages._order vs the story titles recorded in coverageSweep.
flags.detail: Storybook files Icon button, Toggle button and Read more under Components/Data Display, Link under Components/Navigation, and Dialog under Components/Feedback. The Figma pages file them by design semantics instead: Icon button, Link and Read more on Actions; Toggle button on Inputs; Dialog on Surfaces & navigation. Storybook's Data Display group is doing duty as a catch-all — it also holds Divider, Typography and the Icon catalogue — so it is a weak signal of what a component is.
flags.handling: Design semantics chosen by Daniel 2026-08-03 when the two taxonomies were put side by side. Recorded, not normalised: this is a code↔design disagreement of the same kind as the four list-row surfaces. Anyone navigating between Storybook and the Figma file should expect these five to sit in different groups.

flags.summary: The facesheet card header divider is written as an sx CSS shorthand with a theme path inside it, so the whole declaration is invalid and no divider renders.
flags.where: facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx:217 and facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/CardLayout.tsx:170 — the only two occurrences of this pattern in the monorepo.
flags.detail: sx={{ borderBottom: "1px solid background.default", height: "3rem" }}. In sx, a full CSS shorthand string is passed through verbatim; only standalone properties like borderColor resolve theme paths. 'background.default' is not a valid CSS <color>, and an invalid value inside a shorthand invalidates the entire declaration, so border-bottom is dropped rather than falling back to a default colour. The intended colour is background.default = #E8E5DF (Backbone 3).
flags.effect: Two of the eight header bands are the only ones that ask for a divider, and neither draws one. The rendered result is identical to the six clinical-system bands, which makes the divergence invisible in a browser and only findable in source — exactly the case the 'never measure from a rendered component' rule protects against.
flags.fix: borderBottom: 1, borderColor: 'background.default' — or a theme callback: borderBottom: (t) => `1px solid ${t.palette.background.default}`.
flags.handling: Reported, not fixed — web-app-v2 is a read-only reference checkout. Do NOT draw a divider on the Figma band until Daniel decides whether the divider or its absence is the intended design; six of eight sites currently ship without one.

flags.summary: One facesheet card implementation sets CardContent paddingBottom to 128px where its twin sets 16px, because a bare number in sx is a spacing multiple, not pixels.
flags.detail: facesheet-ui writes sx={{ paddingBottom: 16 }}. paddingBottom is in paddingKeys (@mui/system/esm/spacing.js:43), so it routes through createUnaryUnit(theme,'spacing',8,'spacing') (spacing.js:85). theme/theme.ts passes createTheme only palette, typography and components — no spacing key — so createSpacing falls back to its default of 8 (createTheme/createSpacing.js). 16 x 8 = 128px. The clinical-system twins write sx={{ padding: "0 16px 16px 16px" }}, a string, which is taken literally as 16px.
flags.effect: The same card surface has an 8x difference in bottom padding between two live implementations. 128px is almost certainly not intended — the number 16 reads as pixels at a glance, which is how it survived.
flags.handling: Reported. Relevant to Figma only insofar as the card content padding must not be transcribed from facesheet-ui; use the clinical-system 0/16/16/16 values, which match the MUI substrate's 16px.

flags.summary: ImmunizationsCard hardcodes the drawer card style but still renders the fullscreen-only header band, so in fullscreen it is the only facesheet card with no elevation and no min-height.
flags.detail: Its six siblings wrap in StyledCard (Facesheet.tsx:21-27), which branches on layout: FULLSCREEN gives minHeight 10rem, anything else gives boxShadow none. ImmunizationsCard instead writes <Card sx={DRAWER_CARD_STYLE}> where DRAWER_CARD_STYLE = { boxShadow: 'none' } (types/facesheet.ts:203-205) — unconditionally — and then gates its CardHeader on layout === FacesheetLayout.FULLSCREEN. So in fullscreen it shows the title band on a flat, short card while every sibling is elevated and at least 160px tall.
flags.handling: Reported. Does not change the band spec itself.

flags.summary: Five facesheet cards exist in two live implementations in different packages, and the two disagree on the divider, the content padding and whether the header renders at all.
flags.where: clinical-system/src/components/Facesheet/Cards/* (consumed by FacesheetDrawer.tsx and FacesheetPage.tsx) vs facesheet-ui/src/components/Card/FacesheetCard.tsx (consumed by facesheet-ui CardLayout.tsx).
flags.detail: Medications, Vitals, Labs, Problems and History are implemented in both. clinical-system additionally has Immunizations and Allergies; facesheet-ui additionally has Recommendations and Supplements. Divergences: (a) facesheet-ui declares a header divider, clinical-system does not; (b) facesheet-ui's CardContent bottom padding resolves to 128px, clinical-system's to 16px; (c) clinical-system gates the header band on FULLSCREEN layout, facesheet-ui renders it always; (d) clinical-system's AllergiesCard renders no band at all.
flags.handling: Reported as a disagreement, not normalised — this is the fifth recurring-surface finding after the four list-row surfaces, the five interactive states, the five disabled greys and the six link treatments. Which implementation is canonical is a product question. The Figma band should be built once, from the shared geometry (48px, h2/primary, 16px horizontal), with the divider left off until the question is settled.

flags.summary: There is no MuiCardHeader, MuiCardContent or MuiCardMedia override anywhere, so every card-header decision lives in per-site sx.
flags.where: packages/design-system/src/overrides — CardOverrides.ts, CardActionsOverrides.ts and CardActionAreaOverrides.ts are the only Card-family files.
flags.detail: MuiCard sets defaultProps only (variant elevation, square false, raised false). MuiCardActions sets justifyContent flex-end. MuiCardActionArea sets disabled true — open decision 4. Nothing themes the header. The 48px band, the h2 primary title and the divider are therefore product conventions, not design-system truth.
flags.handling: This is the finding, not a defect: the header band is a de facto pattern with no home in the theme. If it is meant to be a design-system component, the theme is where it should live. Recorded for Daniel to decide; see components.CardHeaderBand for the buildable spec.

flags.summary: The primary nav bar renders under createPartnerTheme, never under the canonical design-system theme, so no part of it is design-system truth.
flags.where: navigation-ui/src/root.component.tsx:37 mounts CobrandedApp; navigation-ui/src/components/CobrandedApp.tsx wraps App in ThemeProvider with the cobranding theme; navigation-ui/src/context/CobrandingContext.tsx defaults to createPartnerTheme('tebra').
flags.detail: createPartnerTheme (design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts) builds a distinct theme that remaps palette.action.hover, palette.text.primary, palette.background.paper and palette.divider from a NavigationPalette, and adds the only MuiToolbar override in the entire system. schema.decisions.1_sourceOfTruth already scopes src/cobranding out as 'partner navigation chrome only'. The consequence had not been drawn: it puts the whole primary nav outside the design system.
flags.decisionNeeded: Whether the nav bar belongs in the Figma library at all. If yes, cobranding must come into scope and the library gains a second palette with six base themes. If no, the nav should be named explicitly as out of scope on the Cover so it stops resurfacing.
flags.handling: Reported, not resolved — this is a scope question for Daniel. Spec captured in components.PrimaryNavBar in case the answer is yes. UPDATE 2026-08-03: the Tebra-default nav was built anyway, as its own section with every component description carrying the 'renders under createPartnerTheme, not the design-system theme' provenance line. Building it does not answer the scope question — it makes the answer visible. The six-theme surface stays out of the canonical claim.
flags.status: BUILT 2026-08-03 under the scope caveat; publish still gated.

flags.summary: Three nav colours have no home in paletteValues.ts — the same class of finding as the hardcoded Chip hexes.
flags.detail: #195b63 (navIconHoverBackground and submenuBackground and searchResultsBackground), #002328 (searchInputBackground) and #003840 (primaryDark) return zero matches in palette/paletteValues.ts. #004852 and #417E86 do resolve, to Growth 1 and Growth 2. So the Tebra nav is two-thirds palette colours and one-third values that exist only in the cobranding file.
flags.handling: Recorded. If the nav is brought into scope these three need either promotion to the palette or the same 'hardcoded (no palette)' treatment the Chip hexes got on the Tokens page.

flags.summary: Clicking the user avatar opens a completely empty MUI Menu on top of the real hover-driven user menu.
flags.detail: <Menu anchorEl={userMenuAnchor} open={Boolean(userMenuAnchor)} onClose={handleUserMenuClose} ...></Menu> has no children. The avatar's onClick is handleUserMenuOpen, which sets userMenuAnchor and therefore opens this empty Menu — an empty paper plus a modal backdrop that has to be dismissed. The actual UserMenuContent is delivered separately through NavIconButton's menuContent prop, which renders it in its own hover-driven Popper. So the click path and the hover path are different mechanisms and the click path renders nothing.
flags.handling: Reported. Either give the Menu its UserMenuContent children or drop it and the userMenuAnchor state entirely, since the Popper already covers the interaction.

flags.summary: Four console.log calls ship in the navigation render path, three of them explicitly labelled Debug.
flags.where: navigation-ui/src/context/CobrandingContext.tsx (three, inside the useMemo, logging active partner, partner config and theme.palette.primary) and navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx onClickAwayListener (console.log(event.target)).
flags.detail: The CobrandingContext trio run on every partner change and are preceded by the comment '// Debug: log active partner and theme colors'. The Navigation one fires on every click-away while the mobile search is open.
flags.handling: Reported. No visual consequence.

flags.summary: The nav mixes a magic-number media query with theme breakpoints, and forces a 64px bar at every width instead of MUI's responsive 56/64.
flags.where: navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx — isDesktopNav uses useMediaQuery('(min-width:1100px)') while isSmUp uses theme.breakpoints.up('sm'); the Toolbar sets sx minHeight:64.
flags.detail: 1100px matches no breakpoint in the theme, so the desktop/drawer switch cannot be reasoned about from the token set and will not move if breakpoints are retuned. Separately, theme.mixins.toolbar gives 56px below sm and 64px at sm and up; the sx minHeight:64 flattens that, so the mobile bar is 8px taller than the substrate intends.
flags.handling: Recorded. Relevant to Figma only if the nav comes into scope — it means one 64px bar covers every breakpoint, which simplifies the build.

flags.summary: The partner theme's nav icon hover-colour rule does nothing in five of the six base themes, including Tebra's.
flags.where: design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton root — '&:hover svg { color: submenuText }' — against baseThemes.ts.
flags.detail: The rule swaps the glyph from navText to submenuText on hover. In tebra-default, blue-dark, blue-light, green and orange both values are #ffffff, so nothing changes; only gray-light differs (navText #969696, submenuText #ffffff). The visible hover feedback in every other theme comes from the background swapping to navIconHoverBackground, not from the glyph.
flags.handling: Recorded as a dead-rule finding in the same family as ToggleButtonOverrides' JSS ref syntax — valid and executing, but with nothing to do. Not a defect; it exists for gray-light.

flags.summary: The nav bar renders 65px, not 64px — the discovery pass recorded 64 and wrongly dismissed the legacy library's 65.
flags.where: navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx Toolbar sx minHeight:64, against design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton.styleOverrides.sizeLarge { height: "65px", width: "65px" }.
flags.detail: minHeight is a floor, not a fixed height. The Toolbar is display:flex with align-items:center and no height cap, so a 65px child expands it. Every top-level nav item and every right-cluster utility is an IconButton at size='large', so the 65px always applies and the bar is always 65px. The 64px figure only describes a bar containing nothing 65px tall, which never occurs.
flags.correctsFlag: components.PrimaryNavBar crossReference, which claimed 65 was a legacy-library value rather than source.
flags.whyItWasMissed: The discovery pass read Navigation.tsx for the bar and NavIconButton.tsx for the button, but took sizeLarge from neither — it lives in createPartnerTheme.ts, a third file. Re-reading all three under standing rule 6 surfaced it.
flags.handling: Figma is built at 65px. Both figures are recorded on the Nav / Bar description so the 64 in source is not mistaken for a Figma error.
flags.status: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-03 by navBarHeightDrivenBySearchNotButtons. The 64->65 correction was right as far as it went; 65 is still wrong for the desktop bar.

flags.summary: The partner theme silently REPLACES two canonical styleOverrides roots rather than merging with them, because both sides are functions.
flags.where: design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton.root and MuiMenuItem.root, against overrides/IconButtonOverrides.ts and overrides/MenuItemOverrides.ts.
flags.detail: createPartnerTheme calls createTheme(defaultTebraTheme, partnerThemeOverrides), which deep-merges. deepmerge cannot merge two functions, so the later one wins outright. Consequences: the nav's IconButton loses the canonical color grey[600], the canonical hover/active background rule and the disabled grey[500]; the nav's MenuItem loses the canonical focus-visible treatment entirely (white ground, 3px primary.main border, radius 4) and its Mui-selected rules. Sibling keys survive normally — sizeSmall, colorPrimary and colorError are plain objects and merge, which is why the replacement is easy to miss.
flags.effect: The file's docstring says only navigation-specific styles are overridden and all standard component overrides are preserved. For these two roots that is not what happens.
flags.handling: Reported, not resolved. It is why Nav / Icon button and Nav / Menu item are built as separate components rather than variants of the canonical ones — the divergence is structural, not cosmetic.

flags.summary: Tokens page group captions did not wrap, so any caption longer than the 1272px content width was silently clipped.
flags.detail: mkText leaves textAutoResize at its WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT default, so the caption grew past the frame; the page root sets clipsContent true, so the overflow was invisible rather than obviously broken. Surfaced when the hardcoded (no palette) caption was extended to name createPartnerTheme.
flags.fix: Generator now sets textAutoResize 'HEIGHT' and layoutSizingHorizontal 'FILL' on every group caption. Applied to the generator on disk and to the rendered page, so it cannot recur.
flags.handling: Fixed at source, not just on the page.

flags.summary: The desktop nav bar is 76.8px, not 65px — the inline patient search column is taller than the 65px icon buttons and sets the Toolbar height.
flags.where: navigation-ui/src/components/PatientSearch/PatientSearch.tsx wrapper Box p:2 and TextField sx, against Navigation.tsx Toolbar sx minHeight:64.
flags.detail: Derivation, every term from source: InputBase input height 1.4375em = 23px (InputBase.js:127, boxSizing content-box) + OutlinedInput size-small padding 8.5px top and bottom (OutlinedInput.js:113) = 40px input; + the PatientSearch sx "&& .MuiInputBase-root { padding: 0.3 }" = 0.3 x 8 = 2.4px each side = 44.8px; + the wrapper Box p:2 = 16px each side = 76.8px. The Toolbar is align-items:center with only a minHeight floor, so its height is max(left cluster 65, right cluster 76.8) = 76.8. Below sm the inline search is not rendered (isInlineSearchVisible = isSmUp) and the bar falls back to 65px.
flags.whyItWasMissed: Two passes read the Toolbar and the icon button and stopped there. The height is actually set by a component in a different package folder that neither pass opened.
flags.handling: Figma is built at 76.8px. Both breakpoint heights recorded on the Nav / Bar description.
flags.correction: The arithmetic was right and the conclusion was wrong. Summing the search wrapper's 32px padding onto the 44.8px field assumed the toolbar stacks its children's box heights; a flex toolbar with align-items:center centres them instead. The search column never forces the bar to 76.8 — it centres inside whatever height the bar is. Rendered product is 65px. Superseded by components.PrimaryNavBar.geometryRuling (Daniel, product-rendered authority).
flags.lesson: A derivation can be arithmetically sound and still describe something that never renders. For layout that depends on flex behaviour, the rendered product outranks the computation.

flags.summary: The nav surfaced the first authored-fractional dimensions in the build; resolved by rounding to whole numbers with the computed value recorded.
flags.where: Nav / Bar 1440x76.8, Nav / Search 400x76.8 with a 44.8px field, Nav / Logo 100x23.88, Icon / Payments inner glyph 24x18.24.
flags.detail: Three independent sources, none of them an authoring choice. (1) The 0.3 spacing multiplier in PatientSearch's TextField sx resolves to 2.4px and propagates to 44.8 and 76.8. (2) The Tebra wordmark's viewBox ratio 186.82/782.49 at the declared 100px width gives 23.88. (3) PaymentsIcon's 25x19 viewBox in a 24x24 box gives 18.24. Every previous fractional value in this build was a pxToRem inflation with an intended integer behind it, which the rule handles by binding the integer and recording computedPx. These have no intended integer — the fraction IS the value.
flags.handling: Resolved. No further height or geometry archaeology on the nav; the investigation is frozen. The sub-sm bar height stays 65px and is exact.
flags.resolution: Daniel, as design authority, ruled on 2026-08-03: round each fractional value to its nearest integer and record the true computed value as computedPx, per the same convention already used for pxToRem inflation. Applied — bar 76.8 -> 77, search column 76.8 -> 77, search field 44.8 -> 45, search text inset 16.4 -> 16, wordmark 23.88 -> 24, Payments glyph 18.24 -> 18 at y 2.88 -> 3. The allDimensionsInteger invariant is restored file-wide. This is recorded as a DESIGNED DECISION (source: Daniel, this pass), not a transcription — the Figma values are deliberately not the computed values, and every departure is documented in the component description and here.
flags.amendment: The standing rule is amended rather than broken: authored-fractional sources get ROUNDED-WITH-RECORD, not preserved. Previously the rule only contemplated pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer existed behind the fraction. It now covers the case where no intended integer exists — the fraction is still not carried into Figma, and computedPx still carries the truth.

flags.summary: The Tebra wordmark hardcodes its fill in a <style> block, so it is the one bar element that cannot respond to a partner theme.
flags.detail: #f7f4eb appears nowhere in packages/design-system, and is one step off illustrationCream #F8F3EB without being it. Every other glyph in the bar uses currentColor and therefore follows navText. Recorded as color/hardcoded (no palette)/navLogoCream — a fourth nav orphan alongside #195b63, #002328 and #003840.
flags.handling: Transcribed as authored. Not a defect for Tebra-default, where the cream reads correctly on Growth 1 — but a partner using a light nav ground would get a near-invisible wordmark, which is presumably why PartnerLogo swaps the whole component for an for non-Tebra partners.

Against the legacy list: 'app switcher' is Platform under another name; 'reports' is the analytics item, whose config id is analytics but whose glyph component is ReportsIcon; 'patients' and 'history' have NO nav slot at all — patients are reached through the inline search, and there is no history item in the config; 'engage' ships in source but is absent from the legacy list; 'mail' and 'help' are right-cluster utilities, not nav slots.

flags.summary: Button's Size default was reported done but had not changed — the reorder moved child order, and Figma reads canvas position.
flags.detail: Verification found children[0] = Size=Medium while defaultVariant was still Size=Small at (32,32), with Size=Medium parked at (662,32). An instance placed from the set resolved to Size='Small'. That signature is what a layers-panel drag produces: it reorders children[] and leaves x/y untouched, so nothing visibly changes on canvas and the default does not move.
flags.resolution: Fixed 2026-08-03 by swapping the Small and Medium column blocks horizontally: Button delta 630 (Small 32->662, Medium 662->32), 36 nodes moved; Button group / Segment delta 450 (Small 40->490, Medium 490->40), 36 nodes moved. Grid structure preserved — only the two blocks exchanged x, rows and state columns untouched. Verified by INSTANCE read, not master read: both sets now resolve Size to 'Medium'. 0 overlaps, 0 fractional positions, set bounds unchanged.
flags.whyItWasMissed: It was reported complete and looked complete. Only an instance-level read caught it — the same failure mode standing rule 1 exists for, applied to a variant default rather than a paint.
flags.handling: Resolved. The API behaviour is recorded in figmaBuild.pluginApiNotes so the next default change does not repeat it.

flags.summary: Button group / Segment had the same Size default inversion as Button, and had never been flagged.

flags.detail: The story default is medium and MUI's own ButtonGroup default is medium, but the Figma set's defaultVariant was Size=Small and an instance resolved to Small. flags.summary: The search magnifier is a trailing adornment in source; the review note described it as leading.

There is no startAdornment anywhere in the component. forcePopupIcon={false} and disableClearable remove the dropdown arrow and clear button, so the magnifier is the only adornment and it sits on the RIGHT.

flags.handling: Built trailing. If the product genuinely renders it leading, that is a code/product divergence worth its own look — but nothing in this component produces a leading magnifier.

flags.summary: There is no history or clock slot in the primary nav bar. The history-shaped thing in the product is the Recent patients panel inside the search dropdown.
flags.detail: Checked five ways after the height saga's lesson about trusting absence. (1) navigation.config.ts declares exactly six items: platform, clinical, billing, engage, tebraPayments, analytics. (2) useNavigation merges those six ids with six dynamic hooks and nothing else — there is no seventh slot and no fallthrough. (3) A monorepo-wide grep for AppBar and <Toolbar across every package returns ONE file, Navigation.tsx, so there is no second bar rendering alongside. (4) No nav-item registry or injection mechanism exists; messages-ui's NavigationConfig is its own side menu, not the primary bar. (5) useRecentChartsQuery — the only history-shaped data in navigation-ui — is consumed ONLY by PatientSearch, where recentCharts become recentPatientOptions and render as a 'Recent patients' subtitle2 heading plus a Divider inside the search dropdown when the input is under two characters. No icon, no clock, no bar slot. UserMenuContent carries only OpenInNewIcon.
flags.conclusion: Absence confirmed by positive evidence, not by a failed grep. The observation was real; the element is the Recent patients panel in the search dropdown, which is not built (only the closed field is).
flags.handling: Reported either way as asked. Nothing added to the bar. The Recent patients dropdown panel is a candidate if the search states are ever built out.

flags.summary: The nav avatar is built as initials, but initials are the product's fallback — the typical fill is an illustrated persona SVG.
flags.detail: Navigation renders <Avatar src={userImageUrl}>{userInitials}</Avatar>; on image error it swaps to getDefaultUserImage(hasRole(ROLES.Provider)), which returns /shared-assets-ui/bundle/css/img/chrome/persona/provider-tebra-bg.svg or staff-tebra-bg.svg. The initials child only surfaces when the image itself fails to load. So the typical avatar is illustrated content chosen by role, and the built Content=Letter variant represents the fallback.
flags.handling: Recorded on the Nav / Bar description rather than rebuilt: the persona SVGs are runtime assets in shared-assets-ui, outside packages/design-system, and are not transcribed. Content=Letter stays as the built representation.

flags.summary: The nav has no separate Selected state — hover, focus and menu-open are one flag and one paint.
flags.detail: showActiveBackground = isActive || isButtonFocusedOrHovered, where isActive means the popper menu is open. All three conditions produce the same #195b63 ground, and nothing in the component or the partner theme distinguishes a selected or current-route item — NavItem takes no active prop and there is no route matching in the bar.
flags.handling: Built as State=Hover, which stands for all three. The REFERENCE frame now carries a callout on the anchor slot naming it SELECTED (menu open) and stating that it is the same paint as Hover, so the state is discoverable without implying a variant that does not exist. Requested by Daniel's review; the honest form was a label rather than a new variant.

flags.summary: The nav icon buttons explicitly remove the global focus-visible outline, so keyboard focus in the nav is indicated only by a background change identical to hover.
flags.detail: CssBaselineOverrides gives every focusable element `*:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid primary.main }`. NavIconButton overrides it with `'&&&&': { outline: 'none' }` — quadrupled specificity, so it wins decisively. Focus still sets showActiveBackground via onFocus, so the button does gain the #195b63 ground, but that is the same paint as hover and carries no ring. A keyboard user cannot distinguish a focused nav button from a hovered one.
flags.handling: Reported, not resolved. Figma models it as built — Nav / Icon button has no Focus visible variant precisely because the code has no distinct focus visual. Listed under notGaps in the focus enumeration for that reason.

items.title: Button hierarchy
items.verbatim: Contained primary is white with a core border; contained secondary is the visually filled action. Decide whether to keep this semantic inversion.
items.note: Independently transcribed from ButtonOverrides.ts: containedPrimary is common.white with a core.main border, containedSecondary is filled secondary.main. The Figma Button reproduces the inversion faithfully. This is an open DESIGN question, not a transcription error — the build documents the fact but does not resolve the question.

items.title: Radio integration defect
items.verbatim: The override is registered as MuiRadioButton, not MuiRadio. Figma should not depict custom behavior until the executable theme is corrected.
items.note: NEW TO THIS BUILD — not previously caught. MuiRadioButton is not a valid MUI component key, so RadioButtonOverrides.ts is dead code and Radio renders unthemed. Needs verification against the checkout and a code fix. Radio is not built in Figma, so nothing here depicts it.

items.title: Outlined input border
items.verbatim: The theme inherits MUI's light outline; the sticker sheet expects a darker Synapse 1 outline. Encode one shared decision on MuiOutlinedInput.
items.note: Matches flags.autocompleteUnthemedGeometry. The Autocomplete / Field default outline is bound to color/substrate/inputOutline = rgba(0,0,0,0.23), MUI's own value, because no MuiOutlinedInput override exists. If the Synapse 1 outline is the intent, it is a code change and the Figma variable follows.

items.title: Passive cards
items.verbatim: MuiCardActionArea is disabled by default. Interactive cards need an explicit product decision and accessible affordance.
items.note: Card is not built in Figma. Carried forward untouched.

items.title: Chip color governance
items.verbatim: Success and error interactions contain hard-coded colors. Replace them with named semantic tokens before publishing components.
items.note: Same finding as flags.chipRawHex — ChipOverrides.ts hardcodes #C3E7C0 (colorSuccess) and #FD919F (colorError hover), neither in paletteValues.ts. Not on the Autocomplete path, which uses outlinedPrimary, so the built Tag is unaffected. CORRECTED 2026-08-03: both hexes ARE Figma variables — color/hardcoded (no palette)/chipSuccessBackground and color/hardcoded (no palette)/chipErrorClickableHover, each carrying the literal hex as its code syntax. Verified by enumerating the live Tebra/Color collection. Neither has a home in paletteValues.ts, which is the part that remains true.

standingBatchRules._purpose: Non-negotiable checks every future batch runs before reporting. Added after the paint-opacity defect reached four already-signed-off components.
standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification: Place ONE INSTANCE of every new variant and read its RENDERED paints — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — comparing each against its master. Master-level reads are NOT evidence: paint-level opacity renders correctly on a master and incorrectly on an instance, which is exactly how the defect survived four batches. Any alpha must live in the variable's stored rgba, never as paint-level opacity. SCOPE: that last sentence governs UNBOUND paints only - for a BOUND paint Figma surfaces the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity, and that mirrored value is correct; read rule 9_boundPaintAlpha before touching it.
standingBatchRules.2_unboundPaintAudit: Walk EVERY top-level node on EVERY page, not just component sets. Reference frames, notes frames and loose glyphs count. Auditing only component sets is what let 3 unbound paints sit in the Radio reference frame across several batches.
standingBatchRules.3_referenceCounts: Count componentPropertyReferences per variant after any clone or combineAsVariants — cloning a variant inside a set silently drops them all.
standingBatchRules.4_skipInvisibleFalse: Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any audit walk, so boolean-hidden slots are inspected.
standingBatchRules.5_opacityLast: If paint-level opacity is genuinely unavoidable somewhere, apply it as the final operation AND verify on an instance. Prefer promoting to a computed variable.
standingBatchRules.6_enumerateDontRecall: When remediating or sweeping, enumerate from the file rather than from a previously reported list. The alpha remediation's known list was missing 18 of 48 paints.
standingBatchRules.7_fileIdentityFirst: Every Figma call passes fileKey YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw explicitly — never rely on an ambient or last-used file. Every session's FIRST Figma action verifies file identity against this schema's page inventory (figmaBuild.pages._order) before any read informs a decision or any write occurs; if the page list does not match, stop and report rather than proceeding. Added 2026-08-03 after a session read the legacy team library (ZPf0sJy83aPyrHjCVHomya, 'Tebra Working UI Kit') and produced a full reorganisation analysis against the wrong file. Note that figma.root.name returns 'Document' for both files, so the file NAME is not a usable identity check — the page list is.
standingBatchRules.8_roundWithRecord: Never carry a fractional dimension into Figma. Two cases, one treatment. (a) pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer exists behind the fraction: bind the intended integer, record computedPx. (b) Authored-fractional sources, where no intended integer exists — a fractional spacing multiplier, a viewBox ratio, a non-square viewBox in a square box: ROUND to the nearest integer and record the true value as computedPx in both the component description and the schema, and label the rounding a design decision with its source and date. Added 2026-08-03 when the primary nav produced the first case-(b) values (76.8, 44.8, 23.88, 18.24); Daniel ruled round-with-record as design authority. Intrinsic geometry is out of scope for this rule: VECTOR and GROUP bounds are the union of their path data, are not authored, and are not rounded — the tier 6 illustrations already set that precedent.
standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha: Before changing ANY paint-level opacity, first check whether that paint has a bound colour variable. If it does, Figma SURFACES the variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity - it does NOT multiply the two. A paint bound to a variable storing rgba(0,0,0,0.87) correctly reads back paint.opacity 0.87 and renders at 0.87; that is the expected state, not a double-alpha defect, and it must be left alone. Forcing such a paint to opacity 1 DISCARDS the alpha and renders the node fully opaque. Rule 1's 'never as paint-level opacity' applies to UNBOUND paints only. Established empirically 2026-08-26 (checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry) after the opposite assumption produced a real regression on Alert filled/warning; reverted and audited library-wide 2026-08-27 (boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27). To re-confirm at any time: bind a rectangle to an alpha-carrying variable, never set opacity, then read paint.opacity back - it returns the variable's alpha.
standingBatchRules.10_cloneDropsPropertyRefs: Cloning a variant to add a new axis value DROPS componentPropertyReferences on every child. The clone keeps its layers and looks correct, but Label/icon-visibility/icon-swap stop responding — instance property values are stored yet never render, so a swapped instance silently shows the component default. After any variant clone, re-apply refs by copying them from a known-good sibling keyed on child layer name, then verify by reading a nested instance rendered characters against its property value, not just the property value. Hit during buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.

focusStateEnumeration._method: Every one of the 34 built component sets enumerated from the Figma file, then crossed against source for whether the component takes keyboard focus. CAPTURE ONLY — closing the gaps is a follow-up batch.
focusStateEnumeration._globalRule: THE KEY FINDING, and it reframes the whole list: focus is styled GLOBALLY, not per component. CssBaselineOverrides.ts:8 sets `*:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid theme.palette.primary.main }` and line 12 sets `*:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none }`. So every focusable element in the system gets a 3px Growth 1 #004852 outline on keyboard focus without its own override doing anything. A component set missing a Focus visible variant is therefore missing a state the theme already gives it — the gap is in Figma, not in the code.

Not a focus visual — it is direct evidence that the GLOBAL outline is expected on Button group segments and had to be rescued from overlap.

overlayRecipe._purpose: Established on Menu. Reuse verbatim for Dialog, Tooltip, Snackbar, Popover and any other floating surface.
overlayRecipe.1_readTheElevation: Find which elevation the component's Paper renders at — read it from source, do not assume. Menu does not set one, so it inherits Popover's `elevation = 8`. Alert uses theme.shadows[3] directly. Autocomplete's paper takes Paper's own default of 1.
overlayRecipe.2_translateTheShadow: MUI's styles/shadows.js builds every elevation from createShadow(...12 numbers) as THREE stacked CSS layers: umbra px[0..3] at rgba(0,0,0,0.20), penumbra px[4..7] at 0.14, ambient px[8..11] at 0.12. Each group is offsetX, offsetY, blur, spread. Map each to a Figma DROP_SHADOW with offset {x,y}, radius = the CSS blur value, and spread passed through. Never eyeball a drop shadow.
overlayRecipe.3_makeItAStyle: Create an effect style named 'Elevation / N' carrying all three layers, and apply it with setEffectStyleIdAsync rather than setting node.effects. The style is the binding — it makes the shadow reviewable and changeable in one place, the way variables do for colour.
overlayRecipe.4_recordProvenance: The Tebra theme passes no `shadows` array, so every elevation is substrate. Say so in the style description and flag it, exactly as with TextField's outline.
overlayRecipe.5_surfaceAndClipping: Paper gets background.paper, radius shape.borderRadius (4), and clipsContent true to mirror overflow:hidden. Check the list/content padding separately — Tebra's global MuiList disablePadding changes it for List-based surfaces but not for styled-div surfaces.
overlayRecipe.6_positioning: Read anchorOrigin and transformOrigin from the component source and draw the composition at that offset. Menu: anchor bottom-left to transform top-left, so no gap. Put the composition on background.default, not white, so the elevation is actually legible.

pluginApiNotes: setBoundVariableForPaint attaches the binding but leaves the paint's raw colour at whatever was passed in; Figma rendered that raw colour, so a paint created as {0,0,0} rendered black despite a correct binding. Fix: write the resolved value into the paint AND bind it. 117 paints were repaired this way.
addComponentProperty with type INSTANCE_SWAP rejects a component publish key and requires the component's node id as defaultValue.
resize() after setting counterAxisSizingMode locks the axis to FIXED — it must be re-set to AUTO afterwards or cloned variants inherit a frozen height.

editComponentProperty cannot change a VARIANT property's defaultValue — the API refuses. The default is fixed by variant ordering at creation time, so order variant values with the code default FIRST when the set is created. Button's Size still defaults to Small because of this.
Instance-swap slots should carry preferredValues so designers get a curated icon list rather than every component in the file.
constraints CANNOT be overridden on an instance ('This property cannot be overridden in an instance'). Set constraints on the icon MASTER; instances inherit. Only fills are overridable per instance.

Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any findAll/walk that must reach boolean-hidden nodes. The first unbound-paint audit reported 0 while blind to the hidden checkbox and clear-icon slots; re-running with the flag false was what exposed them.

Setting an INSTANCE_SWAP property to the component that is ALREADY that slot's default resets the layer's overrides: the layer name reverts from 'Start icon' to the master's name ('Icon / PlusOutlined') and the per-variant colour override is dropped, so the icon falls back to the master's own fill. Only set a swap property when the target differs from the slot default. Mitigated by binding every master's fill to a token (below), so the degraded state is a themed colour rather than a raw hex.

REGENERATING THE TOKENS PAGE: clear the page's children, then derive everything from getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync + getLocalVariablesAsync — never from a hardcoded list, or the page drifts from the variables it documents. Group colour variables by name prefix (color/<group>/...), sort members by name, and read each value with valuesByMode[collection.modes[0].modeId]. Bind rather than paint wherever Figma allows: fills via setBoundVariableForPaint, and setBoundVariable on 'width', 'height', 'topLeftRadius'/'topRightRadius'/'bottomLeftRadius'/'bottomRightRadius' and 'strokeWeight' — all of these accept FLOAT variables and succeeded here. Typography specimens are rendered by applying the real text style with setTextStyleIdAsync, then reading style.boundVariables back to label which variables each style consumes. Keep the brand-alias map in the script (sourced from paletteValues.ts comments) since Figma has no field for it.

Absolutely-positioned children that overhang their parent — a floating notch label at y = -8, an outside focus ring — are CLIPPED by every ancestor auto-layout frame, because Figma frames default to clipsContent: true. Compositions that nest such components inside wrapper columns must clear clipsContent on the wrappers, or the overhang silently disappears. Apply effect styles with setEffectStyleIdAsync rather than assigning node.effects, so the shadow stays reviewable in one place.

setBoundVariable works on FLOAT-valued layout fields — 'width', 'height', 'strokeWeight' and the four corner-radius fields — not just padding and itemSpacing. Useful for documentation pages where a bar's size should BE the token rather than merely depict it.

Paint-level `opacity` on a variable-bound paint is DISCARDED by later structural operations — appendChild, resize, and combineAsVariants all re-resolve the paint from its variable. Apply the opacity as the very last step (Object.assign({}, boundPaint, {opacity})) after the node is in its final position, and verify by reading fills[0].opacity back. Setting opacity before binding never survives at all, because setBoundVariableForPaint returns a new paint.

An INSTANCE_SWAP property resolves to its single defaultValue across EVERY variant in the set, discarding whatever instance each variant was authored with. A variant cannot ship a different default control. Either drop the swap property to keep per-variant instances, or keep the swap and document that one variant renders the wrong default until swapped.

Cloning a variant that is ALREADY inside a COMPONENT_SET silently drops all componentPropertyReferences on the clone and every descendant. Nothing throws and setProperties still records values, so overrides just appear to do nothing. Either add properties after all variants exist, or walk source and clone in lockstep and copy references node-for-node. Always verify by counting references per variant, not by eye.

When a component property drives a hugging container's width (a notch gap sizer, a reserved slot), the sizer must mirror EVERY node that can widen the visible element — a label plus its optional asterisk, not just the label. Test the combination where the optional child is on.

Never fake a border interruption with a background-coloured mask — it only holds on the surface colour you assumed. Build a real gap: a horizontal auto-layout of slices using Figma's per-side stroke weights (strokeTopWeight / strokeBottomWeight / strokeLeftWeight / strokeRightWeight) with corner radii on the end slices. A hugging middle slice sized by a transparent text node bound to the label property makes the gap track content automatically.

Set a TEXT node's `name` AFTER assigning `characters`, and never to the literal 'Text'. 'Text' is the default name for a new TEXT node, so assigning it does not clear the autoRename flag and the content overwrites the name. Prefer type-based or index-based lookup over name-based for text inside components you did not just create.

A TEXT node created with empty characters collapses to width 0, and setting layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' afterwards does NOT recover it — the node stays 0 wide and any text later assigned wraps one character per line (a 'Default Value' string produced a 288px-tall input). Fix: set textAutoResize='HEIGHT', resize() to a real width, THEN set FILL. Verify node.width > 0 before trusting the layout.

Every icon master's vector fill is now bound to the token that already matched its literal value (text/primary, primary/main, grey/600, text/secondary, common/white). Appearance is unchanged, but any lost override degrades to a themed colour and the masters pass the unbound-paint audit.

The variables API lives under figma.variables, NOT on the figma global: getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync and getLocalVariablesAsync are figma.variables.* and throw 'no such property' if called directly on figma.

Auto-layout frames accept minWidth / maxWidth / minHeight / maxHeight, which map onto CSS min/max sizing exactly. Tab's minWidth 90, maxWidth 360 and minHeight 48 are expressed with them rather than by faking a fixed size, so a hugging Tab still grows with its label and still bottoms out at 90.

An ELLIPSE's arcData { startingAngle, endingAngle, innerRadius } reproduces an SVG stroke-dasharray ring exactly, and innerRadius is a 0-1 RATIO rather than a dimension — so a ring whose real thickness is fractional (CircularProgress: 3.273px) can be drawn without storing any fractional value on the node. Angle 0 is 3 o'clock going clockwise, which is also where an SVG <circle> path starts, so the two systems line up with no offset.

CSS `transform: translate(50%, -50%)` on an absolutely-positioned child (Badge's anchorOrigin) keeps the child's CENTRE on the anchor point as it grows. Figma has no equivalent, and a plain absolute child grows rightward from its x. Reproduce it with a centring anchor frame: twice the offset wide, auto-layout with primaryAxisAlignItems CENTER, positioned so its own centre is the anchor point. The child then grows symmetrically. The anchor overhangs the parent, so clipsContent must be false on the component AND on every wrapper that nests it.

figma.combineAsVariants leaves the set in whatever layout you give it; for sets whose variants differ a lot in size, setting layoutMode NONE and positioning variants manually in a size-per-row grid produces a far more reviewable variant sheet than layoutWrap WRAP, which packs them raggedly.

A set-level TEXT component property forces ONE default across every variant, exactly like INSTANCE_SWAP. Adding Title/Body properties to a set whose variants carry different copy silently overwrites all of it with the property default — the variant heights collapse and the axis stops meaning anything. Caught only because the post-combine heights differed from the pre-combine ones. If variants differ by their text, do not expose that text as a property; instance text stays editable without one.
figma.createNodeFromSvg gives its wrapper frame an opaque white fill that the source SVG does not declare. Walking frame.children misses it — walk the frame itself, or clear it explicitly.

createNodeFromSvg DOES accept an embedded base64 data-URI <image>, producing a RECTANGLE with an IMAGE fill, even though createImageAsync is unavailable. Probe with a 1x1 PNG before assuming an illustration must be stripped.

Figma imports an SVG <clipPath> as a mask group and discards the clip shape fill, defaulting it to black. The shape still renders nothing (masks use alpha), but it reads as an unbound black paint in an audit. Bind it to whatever the source declares.

GROUP and BOOLEAN_OPERATION bounds are derived from their contents, so they are fractional whenever the contained geometry is. They cannot be authored to integers and must be excluded from an all-dimensions-integer check, exactly as VECTOR already is.

Set textAutoResize AFTER characters, not before: on a node whose characters are set later, an earlier textAutoResize=HEIGHT does not survive, and the block renders as one unwrapped line. Order is fontName -> characters -> setTextStyleIdAsync -> textAutoResize -> resize.
setTextStyleIdAsync resets textDecoration. Apply UNDERLINE after the text style, and re-apply it after any later characters assignment.

A COMPONENT_SET's default variant is resolved by CANVAS POSITION — the top-left-most variant wins — NOT by child array order. Reordering in the layers panel changes children[] and leaves x/y alone, so the default does not move and the canvas looks unchanged; the set will still report the old defaultValue and instances will still resolve to it. To change a variant default you must move the target variant so it is the top-left node. Confirmed 2026-08-03 on Button, where a layers-panel reorder had put Size=Medium at children[0] while Size=Small stayed at (32,32) and every new instance still came out Small. editComponentProperty cannot change a VARIANT default either — position is the only lever.

resize() on a TEXT node silently resets textAutoResize to 'NONE'. Set the mode AFTER the resize, not before, or the node stops growing with its content — and because it stops growing rather than erroring, the overflow is invisible until an ancestor with clipsContent cuts it off. Cost a clipped REFERENCE note on 2026-08-03; the same shape as the resize()-locks-the-sizing-axis trap already recorded for auto-layout frames.

iconRecipe._why: Took three rounds to converge. Regressing any step visibly breaks icons. Apply to every new icon master and every icon slot.
iconRecipe.1_viewBoxPosition: Vectors must keep their imported viewBox position inside the 24x24 frame — do NOT reset x/y to 0. createNodeFromSvg already positions them correctly; just move them into the component. Verified positions: DownCaret (2, 6.49), Cancel (2, 2), Close-MUI (5, 5), TrashOutlined (2.52, 2), Checkbox (3, 3).
iconRecipe.2_scaleConstraints: Every vector gets constraints {horizontal:'SCALE', vertical:'SCALE'} so the glyph scales like an SVG viewBox. CENTER centres but does not scale, which renders oversized when the frame is set to 16px. Must be set on the master — see pluginApiNotes.
iconRecipe.3_colorInheritance: Figma has no currentColor. Clone the source text paint onto every icon vector per variant, carrying BOTH the resolved colour and the boundVariables together (cloning only the binding reproduces the black-paint gotcha). White knockout shapes inside a glyph must be skipped so they stay white.
iconRecipe.layerNaming: Vector layers must be named 'Vector' — instance-swap overrides only survive across components with matching layer names.

defectsFound.detail: NOT A DEFECT - this entry's reasoning was wrong and the change it describes was a regression. filled/warning binds color/computed (no palette)/alertFilledWarningText (stored rgba 0,0,0,0.87), and its message text and glyph vector each read back paint opacity 0.87. That is NOT a double application: Figma SURFACES a bound colour variable's stored alpha into paint.opacity rather than multiplying the two, so a bound paint reading 0.87 against a variable storing 0.87 renders at 0.87, never at 0.757. Forcing paint opacity to 1 DISCARDED the alpha and left both nodes rendering fully opaque black. Standing rule 1 does not catch this - rule 1 governs UNBOUND paints. See standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha.
defectsFound.status: WITHDRAWN - not a defect. The change made in this pass was a regression; reverted 2026-08-27. See boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27.

checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.defect: In all 12 flush=Left Checkbox variants the hover halo and focus-visible ring were not concentric with the glyph. Offset measured 9px, not 18.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.cause: The halo and ring were never separate objects. The halo is the variant FRAME's own fill (color/computed (no palette)/alphaPrimary04, cornerRadius 21) and the ring is the frame's own 3px OUTSIDE stroke (color/primary/main). flush=Left was implemented by re-padding the frame from [9,9,9,9] to [9,18,9,0]. Total horizontal padding stayed 18 so the frame stayed 42x42 and did not move; auto-layout pushed the GLYPH from x=9 to x=0. So the glyph moved and the halo could not move, because the halo IS the frame.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.whyItCannotBeFixedInPlace: A halo concentric with a glyph at x=0 must extend 9px beyond the frame's left edge - exactly what MUI's negative margin does in CSS. A frame cannot paint outside itself, so the paints had to move onto a child.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.fix: For each of the 12 flush=Left variants: added a 42x42 RECTANGLE named 'Halo' with cornerRadius 21, carried the frame's fill and stroke onto it verbatim (bound variables re-established with setBoundVariableForPaint), cleared the frame's fills and strokes, inserted it at index 0 so it sits behind the glyph, set layoutPositioning ABSOLUTE and positioned it at (-9, 0) so its centre matches the glyph centre (12, 21). clipsContent was already false so the 9px overhang renders.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.preserved: Flush offset unchanged (glyph still at x=0). All 24 variants still 42x42. The 12 flush=None variants untouched - still pad [9,9,9,9], glyph at (9,9), paints still on the frame, no Halo child.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.structuralAsymmetry: flush=Left variants now carry a Halo child; flush=None variants keep the paints on the frame. This is a direct consequence of the instruction not to change the None variants. Making all 24 use the Halo child would be tidier and is the recommended end state.
checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.countCorrection: The report described 'eight flush=Left variants'. There are 12 - checked (3) x State (4). Same for None. 24 total.

alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.test: Bound a rectangle to color/computed (no palette)/alphaPrimary04 (stored alpha 0.04) without ever setting opacity, then read paint.opacity back.
alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.result: paint.opacity read back as 0.04. Figma SURFACES a bound colour variable's alpha into paint.opacity - it does not multiply. A second rectangle with opacity forced to 1 rendered fully opaque, losing the alpha entirely.
alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.consequence: There is NO double-alpha defect in this library. standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification's warning about paint-level opacity is about UNBOUND paints; for bound paints, opacity mirroring the variable alpha is correct and expected.
alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.regressionIntroduced: propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26.defectsFound.alertFilledWarningDoubleAlpha is WRONG and the 'fix' was a regression. Alert variant=filled, severity=warning had its message TEXT and its glyph VECTOR set from opacity 0.87 to 1 while bound to alertFilledWarningText (stored alpha 0.87). Those two nodes now render fully opaque black instead of 87%.
alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.remediation: DONE 2026-08-27 - see boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27. Message text 165:53 restored from paint opacity 1 back to 0.87, with its binding to alertFilledWarningText preserved. The glyph vector I165:50;164:12 needed no change: it was already at 0.87, so the regression had only ever landed on the text node, not on both as this entry assumed. Nothing else on Alert was touched - still 12 variants and 5 component properties.

boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27._status: BUILT, NOT PUBLISHED. namingFreeze._status still reads AWAITING DANIEL'S APPROVAL.
boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27._scope: Revert of one paint opacity on Alert, plus a read-only library-wide audit. Exactly one paint was written. No other component, property, variant or node was modified.
boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27.trigger: checkboxFlushHaloFix2026_08_26d.alphaFindingThatOverturnsAnEarlierEntry.remediation, which was recorded on 2026-08-26 but deliberately not executed in that pass.
boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27.rootCause: propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26 assumed Figma MULTIPLIES a bound colour variable's stored alpha by paint.opacity, and therefore read 'variable alpha 0.87 + paint opacity 0.87' as a double application yielding 0.757. Figma does not multiply: it SURFACES the stored alpha into paint.opacity. The two values agreeing is the correct, expected state. Setting opacity to 1 discarded the alpha instead of correcting it.
