libraryWideAudit.question: Was the same reasoning error applied anywhere else - any node whose paint opacity was forced to 1 while bound to a variable carrying stored alpha?
libraryWideAudit.method: Identified every local COLOR variable whose stored value in any mode has alpha < 1 (17 of 76), then walked every page comparing every fills and strokes paint bound to one of them against that variable's stored alpha. Per-segment text fills read via getStyledTextSegments so mixed-fill TEXT nodes were not skipped.
libraryWideAudit.result: 204 bound-alpha paints, 0 mismatches (counted after the Alert fix; before it, Feedback held the single mismatch).
libraryWideAudit.remoteVariables: 0 paints anywhere in the file bind a non-local variable, so nothing escaped the local-variable list the audit was built from.
libraryWideAudit.touchedComponentsInScope: All five components propertySurfaceRepair2026_08_26 modified were covered - Alert on Feedback; Dialog, Drawer, Menu and Stepper on Surfaces & navigation. Both pages returned clean.
libraryWideAudit.conclusion: Alert's message text 165:53 was the only instance library-wide. The reasoning error was applied once, not repeatedly.
libraryWideAudit.notInScope: This audit compares PAINT-level opacity against bound variable alpha. Node-level opacity is a separate, legitimate mechanism and was not flagged - e.g. Alert's Icon frame 165:49 carries node opacity 0.9, which is MUI's icon treatment and correct.

boundAlphaRegressionRevert2026_08_27.ruleRecorded: standingBatchRules.9_boundPaintAlpha. standingBatchRules.1_instancePaintVerification was also scoped to UNBOUND paints, since its closing sentence read as licence for exactly the change that caused this regression.

buttonInheritColour2026_08_28.openQuestion: Contained + inherit background is version-dependent and still unread. MUI v5 renders it from grey[300] (containedInherit); v6 rewrote Button onto CSS variables (--variant-containedBg) and handles inherit differently. A filesystem-wide search found no vendored copy of @mui/material/Button/Button.js anywhere, and node_modules is not installed, so neither could be read here. The built inherit variants therefore carry no background. Resolve by reading the actual installed Button source per major version before adding one.

defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28._scope: A reusable treatment for marking anything in a composition that does not match what ships. Defined once here so the remaining fourteen compositions follow it.
defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28.problem: Compositions render known defects accurately and distinguish them only in prose. A reader scanning a frame cannot tell a defect from an intentional pattern.
defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28.colourConstraint: The marker may not use red, yellow, orange or green. Marked content is frequently red/yellow/green alerts, chips and status indicators, so a semantic colour would collide. The marker must read as chrome, clearly outside the thing it marks.

treatment.container: Auto-layout VERTICAL, itemSpacing 12, padding 16, cornerRadius 4, strokeWeight 1, dashPattern [6,4]

defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28.structure: Example FIRST, then a header row (chip label + one-line "Fix lives in ..."), then a one-line statement of the difference. The example leads so that a marked example and an unmarked one in the same row share a baseline — with the chip above, a marked cell pushed its example 80-190px below its unmarked siblings.

labels.GAP: the component cannot express it at all — not a rendering difference

defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28.rule: Any example rendering something that does not match what ships sits inside a marker. Correct examples sit outside it. The distinction must be legible without reading a word.
defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28.legend: Every composition using markers carries one line in its header block explaining the dashed panel, so the frame is self-describing.

handDrawnCheck2026_08_31.theCheck: Binary, per frame: is any UI element drawn by hand where a published library component exists? Yes or no. Where yes, name the specific elements.
exemptions: SCAFFOLDING — an element drawn because a Figma instance cannot host children (a listbox that cannot be a Paper, a Menu past its four slots, a Table/Row that cannot take real cells).
ANNOTATION — headers, legends, captions, markers, section labels, anything that describes the frame rather than being an example in it.
INEXPRESSIBLE — a state, variant or content shape no published component can express (a selected ButtonGroup segment, a small-density table cell, a two-line Menu/Item).
handDrawnCheck2026_08_31.reportingRule: Every hand-drawn UI element must be assigned to exactly one of the three exemption categories, or the answer is YES and it is a finding. Say which category each falls in.
handDrawnCheck2026_08_31.whyThisIsBetter: It is what the ratio was a proxy for, it cannot drift, and a wrong answer is falsifiable by looking at the frame.

codeDefectRegister2026_08_31.rule: A GAP is something a Figma component cannot express and stays marked in the frame. A defect is something wrong in packages/design-system or its consumers and goes in the register. Compositions keep marking gaps; they do not gain defect prose.

entries.D1: MuiRadioButton is not a MUI slot (MuiRadio is), so RadioButtonOverrides never applies. 38 files / 98 elements. The file carries only defaultProps, so what is lost is ripple suppression, not styling — radios are the only control in the system that ripple. One-line fix.
entries.D2: outlined is unstyled at the theme layer in THREE components, not two. MuiButton (101 el / 71 files), MuiButtonGroup (4 / 4), MuiAlert (1 / 1). All 37 override files swept; these are the only three. Aggravated by containedPrimary already being a white button with a core.main border, so Tebra contained-primary and MUI stock outlined occupy the same visual niche without being the same thing. Button at 71 files is the widest-reaching defect found.
entries.D3: AlertOverrides has no standardSuccess rule (3 el / 3 files take that path) AND no success key in iconMapping (affects all 5 success alerts). CheckmarkFilledIcon already exists and is exported. Both one-liners.
entries.D4: Split button is published in Figma (627:161, 8 variants) but does not exist in code — no match for *split* anywhere in design-system/src. 8 production files hand-roll it, in 7 packages, with two different caret icons. This is a library-parity defect, not a misuse defect: those files had nothing to import. appointment-workflow-ui/src/components/SplitButton.tsx is a complete reusable implementation sitting in a feature package.
entries.D5: The selected segment state is hand-rolled FIVE times in five packages, not twice. Three hardcode #ffffff, two use a token, a sixth copy is pasted into a .md. Four of the five have no hover rule, so ButtonOverrides.containedPrimary &:hover wins and hovering a selected segment discards its selected appearance — #004852/white flips to #CBDDE0/#004852. EventTypeSelector is the only one that pins hover.
entries.D6: LOWER CONFIDENCE, needs an intent decision. standardWarning borders with secondary.main (#FF8D6E brand orange) rather than warning.main (#FCDE73). Looks deliberate — the yellow is near-invisible at 1px and warning.light equals warning.main, suggesting an unfinished ramp — but it is unmarked either way. 43 warning elements.

captionConvention2026_08_31._scope: The single convention for describing a composition and its sections. Settled across the six built frames; the remaining compositions follow it.
captionConvention2026_08_31.supersedes: tableAssembly2026_08_31.deliberateDeviation, which left "the frame carries BOTH conventions" as an open decision.
captionConvention2026_08_31.whatTheDivergenceActuallyWas: The two conventions were never in conflict — they operate at different levels. libraryRestructure2026_08_26c added a FRAME-level header (What it is / Uses / Varies) to 12 frames. Table assembly additionally carried a SECTION-level caption (Shows / Use when / Not this when / Source) on each of its 12 numbered sections. Comparing "four caption fields" against "three header fields" compared a section to a frame. The real divergence was that only 4 of 14 frames had section captions at all: Table assembly, Selection / bulk action bar, Drawer panel and Data grid toolbar. The five frames built in this batch had none.

theConvention.frameLevel: A "Header — composition" block with What it is / Uses / Varies. Add "Reading this frame" when the frame uses defect or gap markers, per defectMarkerConvention2026_08_28. Add "Supersedes" or "Where to find this" only where they apply. The Varies line ends by naming the section-caption convention, so the frame is self-describing.
theConvention.sectionLevel: Every VARIATION section carries a Caption with exactly four fields in this order: Shows / Use when / Not this when / Source. Anatomy and How to build one do NOT take a caption — they are template sections, not variations. This matches Table assembly, where 12 captions cover 12 numbered sections and neither template section has one.

fieldMeanings.Shows: What the section puts in front of the reader. Absorbs what an unstructured Intro line used to do.
fieldMeanings.Use when: The condition under which this is the right choice.
fieldMeanings.Not this when: The condition under which it is the wrong choice, and what to do instead. This is the field the old Intro form had nowhere to put, and it is the main gain from the change.
fieldMeanings.Source: Where the behaviour comes from — a theme override, a MUI rule, or a production count. Keeps every section traceable, which is the grounding discipline of the whole exercise.

captionConvention2026_08_31.typography: Label: Akkurat LL Bold, fontSize bound to VariableID:74:53 (12), lineHeight 16px, fill bound to VariableID:74:36. Body: Akkurat LL Regular, fontSize bound to VariableID:74:55 (14), lineHeight 20px, fill bound to VariableID:74:37. recommendedFix.whyThisIsNotAReversal: A Stage is not a backdrop. It is a depiction of the product page canvas, and the product page canvas genuinely IS #E8E5DF — that is exactly what beigeSurfaceInvestigation2026_08_31 established from source. dividerScopeDecision.chosen: ONLY the most recent visit gets a divider. The 09 Jan 2026 and 22 Sep 2025 visits render as ordinary Note rows.
dividerScopeDecision.why: Three reasons. First, the chart is answering one question — when did I last see this patient and what has happened since — and one question takes one answer; three bands in an eleven-row ledger is a band every three rows, which turns the device back into the row separator it is trying to stop being. Second, the elapsed statement is only true of the most recent visit; "since the visit on 09 Jan 2026 — 7 events" is a different and less useful claim, and two such counts in one column compete. Third, chunking the whole ledger by visit is a different information architecture, not a divider treatment, and it is not what was asked for.

"Since the last visit on 21 Jul 2026" makes the reader compute six weeks from the date. The brief asked the band to "state elapsed time and volume", and as written it states a date and volume.
betterConstructionNoted.alternative: Putting the duration first delivers the elapsed part directly and keeps the date available: "6 weeks since the last visit — 21 Jul 2026 · 4 events". It also front-loads the number that changes, which is the one worth scanning for.
betterConstructionNoted.secondOrderNote: Reading top-down the reader meets the four events before the band that labels them. The band both closes the group above and introduces the visit below, which is coherent, but a duration-first phrasing would survive that order better because the duration reads as a heading rather than as a caption for what came before.

theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened._status: CONFIRMED ON THE CANVAS. Reported, not fixed, as instructed.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.finding: Yes — the band reads heavier here than the same three cards read on the busy patient.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.mechanism: Two things changed at once. On State 1 the cards competed with a dense ledger of yellow chips and seven teal actions, so they were one voice among several. Here the ledger is deliberately quiet — grey chips, five actions, six empty action cells — so the three cards are the busiest thing on the screen and hold the top third of the page uncontested. A chart whose whole message is "nothing is wrong" opens with three statements of things not done.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.secondMechanism: Equal weight flattens unequal things. A colorectal screening overdue at 58 and an atorvastatin refill the patient may have stopped on purpose are rendered identically. On the busy patient the cards were all genuinely urgent, so uniform weight cost nothing; on this patient it manufactures urgency for at least one of the three.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.whatThisArguesFor: Not a fix in this frame. It argues that the insight band needs either a density rule tied to how much is actually outstanding, or a weight axis on the card so a routine obligation can render lighter than a clinical one. Both are decisions, not corrections.

incidentalFindings.collectPaymentAtZeroBalance: The action row still offers "Collect Payment" while the header reads Balance $0.00. The label was left verbatim because it is one of the five evidenced labels and the action row was out of scope, but on a patient with nothing owed the control is offering an action with no object. Screen logic, not a component defect. FOR DECISION.
incidentalFindings.allergyIconIsTheLoudestThingOnScreen: The red AttentionFilled glyph on "Moderate: penicillin" is the highest-contrast element on a screen whose entire point is that nothing is wrong. An allergy banner is a standing safety fact and should persist, so this is probably correct — but it is worth knowing that severity chrome does not scale down with severity, and on a quiet patient it dominates.

npveRebuild_agentRules_2026-09-04.sectionText:
## Rules for any agent working in these files

Any agent — Claude, Codex, or other — editing the Figma files or this repo follows the same loop. Work that skips it gets audited and may be superseded.

1. Read before touching: this file, then design-system-schema.json for current state. The schema is the record; chat history and your own memory are not.
2. Audit before building: when the current state is uncertain, run a read-only inventory first and report it. Never build onto an unverified state.
3. One batch at a time, with a stop condition stated up front. A batch that grows past its stop condition becomes two batches.
4. Additive only. Nothing is deleted, and nothing is moved, renamed, or superseded without a record saying so. Archives get a README.
5. No invention. If the library and code lack a pattern, mark it (GAP/DEFECT per the convention) and build with what exists. Recreating a source drawing by hand and calling it a component is a false record, which is worse than the gap.
6. Verify in pixels. Screenshot what you built and look at it. Property readbacks are claims; renders are evidence. After editing a component, re-screenshot its live instances and diff.
7. Record every batch: a dated schema record via an apply-*.js script, backup first, findings to flags[]. A batch without a record did not happen and will be treated as suspect.
8. Report per rule 13: full report to disk, short reply, no tables in chat. Change logs in the file are written in plain graphic-design language, not system jargon.
9. When sources disagree or a decision is needed, stop and report. Precedence (code > Storybook render > library > source) resolves facts, not design decisions.
